# dsbevx

> Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real symmetric band matrix A.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsbevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsbevx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsbevx(
    order,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N, kd,
    AB, LDAB,
    Q, LDQ,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK,
    IWORK,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | `'all'`, `'value'`, or `'index'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix in band storage |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `AB`<br>Column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kd + 1`<br>Row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output orthogonal matrix (N-by-N) |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q`<br>Rejects `jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldq < max(1, N)` |
| `vl` | `number` | Lower bound of eigenvalue interval |
| `vu` | `number` | Upper bound of eigenvalue interval<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | Index of smallest eigenvalue (1-based)<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | Index of largest eigenvalue (1-based)<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | Absolute tolerance |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride for `w` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvectors |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z`<br>Rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 7 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output failure indices |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | Stride for `IFAIL` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found;
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found;
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangle of A is stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangle of A is stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kd`: The number of superdiagonals of the matrix A if `UPLO = 'U'`, or the number of subdiagonals if `UPLO = 'L'`. $\mathrm{KD} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.

  On exit, `AB` is overwritten by values generated during the reduction to tridiagonal form. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the first superdiagonal and the diagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T are returned in rows `KD` and `KD`+1 of `AB`, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of T are returned in the first two rows of `AB`.
- `Q`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, the N-by-N orthogonal matrix used in the

  reduction to tridiagonal form.

  If `JOBZ = 'N'`, the array Q is not referenced.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing `AB` to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

  See "Computing Small Singular Values of Bidiagonal Matrices with Guaranteed High Relative Accuracy," by Demmel and Kahan, LAPACK Working Note #3.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: The first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. If an eigenvector fails to converge, then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `kd + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDQ < max( 1, N )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` twentieth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsbevx.ndarray(
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N, kd,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL, offsetIFAIL
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobz` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | 'no-vectors' or 'compute-vectors' |
| `range` | `"all" \| "value" \| "index"` | 'all', 'value', or 'index' |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | 'upper' or 'lower' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `kd` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of super- (or sub-) diagonals<br>Requires `kd ≥ 0` |
| `AB` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>(kd + 1) × N</sub> | **in/out** · Band matrix in band storage |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `AB` |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AB` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output orthogonal matrix from dsbtrd (N-by-N) |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of Q |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of Q |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for Q |
| `vl` | `number` | Lower bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | Upper bound of eigenvalue interval (RANGE='value')<br>Rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` |
| `il` | `integer` | Index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (il < 1 \|\| il > max(1, N))` |
| `iu` | `integer` | Index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, RANGE='index')<br>Rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min(N, il) \|\| iu > N)` |
| `abstol` | `number` | Absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride for w |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for w |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)</sub> | **out** · Output eigenvector matrix |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of first dimension of Z |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of second dimension of Z |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for Z |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 7 * N</sub> | **out** · Workspace (length >= 7\*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ 5 * N</sub> | **out** · Integer workspace (length >= 5\*N) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IWORK |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | Stride for IFAIL |
| ↳ `offsetIFAIL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for IFAIL |

<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;

- `AB`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the symmetric band matrix A, stored in the first `KD`+1 rows of the array. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AB(kd+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{kd}) \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AB(1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kd})$.

If `UPLO = 'U'`, the first superdiagonal and the diagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T are returned in rows `KD` and `KD`+1 of `AB`, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, the diagonal and first subdiagonal of T are returned in the first two rows of `AB`.
- `Q`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, the N-by-N orthogonal matrix used in the

  reduction to tridiagonal form.

  If `JOBZ = 'N'`, the array Q is not referenced.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing `AB` to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( il < 1 \|\| il > max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` seventeenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `5 * N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, then i eigenvectors failed to converge. Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.

</section>

## Notes

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable no-restricted-syntax, stdlib/first-unit-test */

import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dsbevx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsbevx';

// 4x4 symmetric tridiagonal matrix (KD=1), lower band storage:

//   4  1  0  0

//   1  5  2  0

//   0  2  6  3

//   0  0  3  7
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );

const AB = new Float64Array([
	4.0,
	1.0,
	5.0,
	2.0,
	6.0,
	3.0,
	7.0,
	0.0
]);
const Q = new Float64Array( 16 );
const W = new Float64Array( 4 );
const Z = new Float64Array( 16 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 50 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 30 );
const IFAIL = new Int32Array( 4 );

// Compute all eigenvalues and eigenvectors:
const info = dsbevx.ndarray( 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'lower', 4, 1, AB, 1, 2, 0, Q, 1, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, m, W, 1, 0, Z, 1, 4, 0, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0, IFAIL, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info );
console.log( 'M (eigenvalues found):', m[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'Eigenvalues (W):', W );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSBEVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSBEVX computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a real symmetric band matrix A. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

</section>
